title: A barrier coating is not another dissolved corrosion inhibitor
original_forecast: Compare the material-role barrier with bare iron of approximately matched iron mass. A paint-origin accessibility rule should not be reported as an acid-base reaction or as conversion of paint into a corrosion product.
original_limitations: The recipe is 95% resolved iron with unresolved coating. Scratches, film thickness, adhesion and local defects are not resolved, and matching bulk Fe does not match surface area.
lock_qualification: Producer-reported manifest hash; artifact omits raw Cargo.lock bytes.

assessment.model_scope: Matched Fe/water/salt/air/O2 and clocks isolate a declared provenance-owned accessibility barrier from bare-iron oxidation. Independent4Fe:3O2:2Fe2O3 state changes agree with actual extent; unresolved coating/alloy remains, air and retained gas are fully counted. This is the original bounded barrier question, not computed chromium passivation, coating defects, pitting immunity, surface-area matching or calibrated corrosion rate.

reason.en: this iron came in under a complete paint film, and a sound coating simply keeps the water and the oxygen off the steel: no electrolyte on the surface, no cathodic reaction, no cell. That is the whole mechanism, and it is also the whole limitation — paint is a barrier and not a cure. Break the film anywhere and the steel at the break corrodes at the bare-metal rate, with no help from the paint around it, because paint gives no cathodic protection. Zinc does, which is the difference between a chipped painted railing and a scratched galvanised one

reason.en: nothing rusts in this vessel, because there is no oxygen in it. Corrosion needs three things at once — the metal, liquid water and oxygen — since it is a circuit: {name} would give up electrons at the anode, oxygen would take them at the cathode, and the water carries the ions between the two. This bench does not yet draw oxygen from the room into an open beaker, so the oxygen has to be put in the vessel for the slow clock to see it{and_then}
